title: Unified similarity+rerank hosted endpoint PRD and launch playbook
creator: Maya Chen
description: This PRD defines a new hosted inference surface that combines similarity (embeddings) and reranking into a single API call (similarity_rerank). Goal is to reduce network roundtrips for common workflows (retrieve -> embed -> rerank) and offer cost/latency improved defaults while keeping behavioral parity with existing separate embeddings + rerank flows.
problem_statement: Customers that implement retrieval-augmented generation and documents search are performing multiple calls: embedding generation, nearest-neighbor search (customer side or managed), then a rerank/completion call to refine results. This multiplies latency and increases per-result cost. There's also friction mapping top-K from embedding stage into rerank model inputs. We need an API that: 1) reduces client orchestration, 2) preserves auditability and metrics per-step, and 3) supports graceful fallback to existing surfaces.
goals: Provide a single REST endpoint /v1/similarity_rerank that accepts query, optional candidate embeddings or candidate IDs, and returns re-ranked results with per-candidate scores and provenance
Meet P95 tail latency <= 220ms for short queries (<=64 tokens) in hosted default lane
Reduce average customer RTT for typical 10-candidate rerank flows by >= 30% compared to separate embeddings+rerank calls (measured under controlled benchmark)
Expose cost-mode parameter (latency|balanced|cost) that selects quantization/beam/early stopping heuristics
Provide SDK primitives for JavaScript and Python with identical contract to other Redwood surfaces
non_goals: This initiative will not replace advanced customer-managed retrieval pipelines (we will accept candidate_ids only as opaque pointers)
We will not change the existing embeddings or rerank endpoints; those remain fully supported
We will not support multimodal embeddings in first launch
scope: MVP includes API contract, runtime implementation for hosted lane, JS/Python SDK changes, telemetry and dashboards, behavioral regression tests against canonical prompt set, and canary rollout with automatic rollback triggers. Excluded: dedicated/private deployment packaging (follow-up cycle).

acceptance_criteria: API contract documented in PRD and openapi spec merged into repo (github.com/redwood-inference/api-specs PR#1692)
End-to-end test harness that replays 10k canonical queries shows average latency improvement >= 30% vs baseline embedding+rerank pipeline under same hardware profile
Performance SLOs met: P95 <= 220ms for <=64 token queries on hosted default pool across 3 regions (us-west1, us-east1, eu-west1)
SDKs (JS/Python) include new client method similarityRerank() with unit tests and integration smoke tests passing on CI
Telemetry: per-tenant cost breakdown, per-step timing (embed, retrieve-adapter, model-rerank), and per-API error rates visible on console dashboard (dashboard link provided)
Behavioral parity: end-to-end rerank quality measured via eval harness (evals/rerank-suite) must not regress by >1% NDCG@10 against canary baseline on curated prompt set
Security: security review completed and sign-off recorded in PRD (security-approval doc link)
Canary plan and rollback criteria defined and validated with SRE and on-call runbook attached
Docs: Quickstart, migration guide from embeddings+rerank, and pricing implications published in docs site with examples
success_metrics: Adoption: >=20 customers actively using similarity_rerank within 60 days of GA
Cost: Average token-cost per retrieval+rerank flow reduced by >=20% for active customers who switch
Reliability: API error rate maintained <= 0.1% during canary and GA
Quality: NDCG@10 regression <= 1% on held-out eval set post-launch
rollout_plan: Phased rollout with internal dogfood -> small external beta -> regional canary slices -> global GA. Each phase gated by telemetry and quality checks. Canary window 72 hours per slice. Rollforward only after stability and quality thresholds met.
canary_plan: Dogfood: internal teams (Search team, Solutions SEs) for 1 week; collect qualitative feedback
Beta: 5 enterprise customers opt-in, 10% of their traffic routed to similarity_rerank for 2 weeks
Regional Canary: 1% of global traffic routed in us-west1 for 72 hours; monitor latency, errors, NDCG drift
Progressive Ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% over 7 days if no triggers fire
rollback_triggers: P95 latency increase > 25% vs baseline for >30 minutes
Quality regression: evaluated NDCG@10 drop > 2% on live holdout set
Undetected model version mismatch causing degraded outputs or data loss
